skills.trigger: When evaluating a focal opacity in the lung periphery or upper zones to distinguish between parenchymal consolidation and pleural pathology.
steps: Inspect the medial margin of the opacity where it interfaces with the lung parenchyma.
Identify if the margin is convex (bulging inward toward the lung) rather than concave or ill-defined.

Classify a convex medial margin as characteristic of a loculated pleural collection (e.g., empyema), whereas pneumonia typically presents with fluffy, ill-defined, or air-bronchogram-containing margins.

skills.trigger: When assessing the costophrenic angles in the presence of adjacent thoracic opacities.
steps: Examine the lateral costophrenic angle for sharpness versus blunting.
Correlate blunting with the presence of fluid density extending from the hemithorax.
Recognize that concurrent blunting supports a pleural etiology (effusion/empyema) over isolated parenchymal masses or atelectasis which may spare the angle or present differently.
